**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

Section 13.4.1 is a mutual assignment clause that already delivers our preferred position on the material terms that matter to us:
- **Our assignment rights:** AbbVie may assign without Harpoon's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, sale of stock, sale of assets or other transaction of the relevant business; all other assignments are subject to consent "not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed."
- **No vendor exit on our change of control:** nothing in Article 12 (termination) or elsewhere gives Harpoon a termination, re-pricing or altered-rights trigger on an AbbVie Change in Control. The only change-of-control machinery — Section 13.2 (Harpoon notice obligation), plus the Competitor provisions in Articles 2 and 5 — runs in our favour.

Noted in the rationale but not flagged: the clause is symmetrical, so Harpoon may also assign to an Affiliate/successor without our consent, and there is no express bar on assignment to an AbbVie competitor. That sits at the playbook fallback (mutual successor assignment, consent otherwise not unreasonably withheld) and is acceptable, especially given our separate competitor protections triggered by a Harpoon Change in Control.
